spec_match.rationale: Builds the product pattern the feature exists for — many named categories sharing a base — on the real registry/priority surface, with the universal rule attempted exactly and its fallback labelled.

interactive.rationale: Live search over real text nodes, wrap-around next/previous, priority-promoted current match, glossary layer toggle, and a registry-state readout.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises a working find-in-page tool with priority and a shared-chrome rule; all present.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles no-match, sub-2-character queries, registry-absent browsers, overlap resolution via priority, and the universal-vs-fallback base-chrome split.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5174965228929024 and MDN's HighlightRegistry reference.

conformance.rationale: The suite's registry round-trip and priority assertions pin the surfaces this tool depends on alongside the universal-selector contracts.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): 'highlight' found 6 matches with search-match painting rgb(254,240,138) read back from the pseudo-element; next/prev wrapped 1→2 and 2→6; glossary registered 5 ranges and toggled off; no-match message for 'zzzz'; base chrome honestly reported as per-name fallback after the universal SyntaxError; zero console errors; both viewports screenshotted.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts each search run with match counts, the base-chrome mode agreeing with the supports probe, and the registry-missing fallback.

design_system.rationale: Token colours for all highlight categories under black text (AA+), 44px input and buttons, pressed state outlined, no raw hex.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled search input with aria-describedby match counter in a live region, prev/next have accessible names, glossary toggle exposes aria-pressed, the article region is focusable and labelled, and match state is announced as text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800: controls wrap, article scrolls in its own region, zero document overflow, identical behaviour.

openQuestions.title: Compose Highlight.type with assistive-technology semantics
openQuestions.detail: Highlight exposes a type attribute (highlight/spelling-error/grammar-error) intended to drive AT presentation. A future concept could pair type with the universal base rule and document what screen readers actually announce per type, turning the annotator's visual categories into a full accessibility story.

openQuestions.title: Record the single-universal-rule evidence on a 158+/flagged engine
openQuestions.detail: With CSSCustomHighlightUniversalSelector active the base chrome should come from the one ::highlight(*) rule (readout says 'universal'); verify the dotted underline appears on all categories without the per-name list.

guidanceConsulted.query: highlight text ranges in page without extra DOM spans
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: TreeWalker-collected text nodes cached for static content; clear stale highlights before re-registering; use priority for overlap stacking.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Text nodes are collected once (static article); each search deletes the page's own registry names (targeted delete, not clear(), so other pages' highlights survive); search-current carries priority 2 over search-match.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible search input live result count
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Pair inputs with visible labels and announce result counts in a polite live region tied via aria-describedby.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The find field has a <label>, aria-describedby pointing at the role=status match counter, and all updates flow through that live region.

summary: A genuinely working find-in-page product on the shipped registry (6 measured matches, wrap-around navigation, priority overlap, glossary layer), honest about the one unshipped piece: the shared base rule falls back per-name after the universal SyntaxError, and the readout names which mode is active. Cloud headless Chromium 141 verification, both viewports clean.
